title: Microtail latency-cost annotated snapshot
content:
Status: DRAFT - snapshot of an exploratory microtail bench and cost comparison.

Purpose:
- Capture a compact, shareable view of how microtail (sub-second, high-cardinality tail spikes) impacts p50/p90/p99 and per-1k-request cost across three serving configurations.
- Surface quick wins for routing + KV cache heuristics and indicate where more detailed sims are needed.

Quick summary (one-paragraph):
We ran a short, repeatable harness with controlled microtail traffic (bursts of 10–40ms inter-arrival jitter layered on a low baseline) against three model variants: fp16 (baseline), int8-quant (small size wins), and hybrid-quant-prefetch (int8 + small KV prefetch policy). Under identical concurrency and slot allocation, microtail spikes increased p99 by 2.2–6.8x depending on model packing and cache hit rate. Cost-per-1k increased modestly for int8 due to efficiency but rose for fp16 under degraded packing. The hybrid-prefetch profile showed the best combined p99 reduction and cost amortization at realistic KV hit rates (40–60%).

Testbed details (short):
- Hardware: 1x A100-80GB (shared test cluster), CUDA 12.2 kernels, patched runtime v0.87 with microtail telemetry enabled.
- Models: smallchat-base-fp16 (baseline), smallchat-quant-int8 (static quant), smallchat-hybrid-prefetch-int8 (KV-prefetch enabled).
- Workload generator: local harness (python) that emits two-behavior traffic: baseline steady stream (50 qps steady) + injected microtail events (bursts with 200–600 concurrent short sessions, each 1–4 tokens). Burst cadence: 30s on / 90s off, repeated 6x.
- Measurement windows: warmup 120s, 6 burst cycles, cooldown 120s. Metrics captured: latency p50/p90/p99, server-side queuing time, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate, amortized GPU-seconds per 1k requests, token-op cost (relative units).

Workload breakdown (approx):
- Steady baseline: 50 qps (conversational), median request length 12 tokens.
- Microtail burst: 400 short sessions (3 tokens avg), high concurrency, arrives as a tight spike (1–3s crest).

ASCII tables (raw snapshot) - latency percentiles (ms) by model and condition:

| Model                            | Baseline p50 | Baseline p90 | Baseline p99 | Burst p50 | Burst p90 | Burst p99 | KV hit % |
|----------------------------------|--------------|--------------|--------------|----------:|----------:|----------:|---------:|
| smallchat-base-fp16              | 28           | 62           | 210          | 32        | 130       | 1430      | 5%       |
| smallchat-quant-int8             | 24           | 55           | 180          | 26        | 110       | 980       | 20%      |
| smallchat-hybrid-prefetch-int8   | 26           | 58           | 150          | 27        | 85        | 220       | 48%      |

Interpretation notes on table above:
- fp16 baseline p99 balloons enormously during microtail (1430 ms) — indicates slot fragmentation + cold-path kernel overheads.
- int8 reduces absolute p99 but still suffers during peak due to packing breakup and KV uncached misses.
- hybrid-prefetch reduces p99 dramatically (to ~220 ms) because short sessions hit prefetched KV or are absorbed into small dedicated tiles; higher KV hit % is the key lever.

Cost snapshot (amortized, USD-equivalent per 1k requests, rough translation):
- fp16 baseline: $3.60 / 1k (steady) -> $4.85 / 1k (during burst windows due to lower effective packing)
- int8: $2.10 / 1k (steady) -> $2.75 / 1k (burst)
- hybrid-prefetch-int8: $2.45 / 1k (steady) -> $2.70 / 1k (burst)

Relative efficiency chart (text sparkline, lower is better cost per 1k):
- fp16 : ▁▂▃▅▇ (large spike during bursts)
- int8  : ▁▁▂▃▅ (smaller spike)
- hybrid: ▁▁▁▂▂ (well controlled)

Microtail-specific observations (short bullets):
- Tail effects are primarily due to two mechanisms: 1) slot fragmentation (small sessions preventing good batching), 2) occasional kernel cold-paths on long sequences when mixed with short requests.
- KV cache helps only if prefetching policy aligns with session boundary (micro-tail sessions are short; prefetching by intent or first token works better than simple prefix caching).
- Packing heuristics matter: opportunistic merging of short sessions into transient mini-batches reduces p99 at little cost; current scheduler treats small sessions conservatively, which is suboptimal during spikes.
- Int8 quantization reduces raw GPU time, but packing loss under contention erodes some gains. Hybrid approach trades a small steady cost for big tail reductions.

Mini ASCII chart: p99 vs KV-hit% (illustrative trend)
KV-hit% -> p99 (ms) for hybrid-prefetch-int8
0%  : █████████████████  (≈1500 ms)
20% : ████████████      (≈650 ms)
40% : ████████          (≈320 ms)
60% : ████              (≈180 ms)
80% : ██                (≈120 ms)

Actionable quick experiments (next 2 sprints):
1) Scheduler tweak: enable optimistic micro-batching for sessions <= 6 tokens and measure p99 at 1% traffic sample. (owner: Ethan)
2) Prefetch policy A/B: first-token intent prefetch vs prefix heuristic. Track KV hit delta and p99 improvement. (owner: Liu)
3) Admission gate: soft limit for microtail floods to preserve high-priority SLOs; simulate 5% throttling and observe user-level metrics. (owner: Priya)
4) Cost model update: incorporate dynamic packing loss fraction into per-route cost projections in Console. (owner: Maya)

Open questions / unresolved:
- How representative are our microtail shapes vs customer traces? Need to pull 2 weeks of production tail traces and run offline replay.
- Is there a measurable user-experience quality delta when we apply soft admission (drop or delay some short sessions)? Need product feedback.
- Prefetch warmup overhead: how often does prefetching itself create transient load that worsens tails? (requires microbench)

Appendix: commands and reproducibility notes (short)
- harness: infra/bench/harness/microtail_runner.py --model smallchat-hybrid-prefetch-int8 --burst-profile bursts.yaml --capture p50,p90,p99,pack-stat
- snapshot artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/microtail/2029-09-17/{raw-logs,kv-frames,tracewalk} (partial)
- runtime tag: v0.87-microtail-exp (includes microtail telemetry feature)

Notes to self (scratch):
- This is intentionally concise; turn into a more visual one-pager for Product with the ASCII charts converted to small sparkline PNGs.
- Push a small replay job to workspace/bench/prod-replay for one prod-tenant to validate shapes.

End of snapshot.
